[kimi @cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6] verdict=fail; failed checks: source_identity, completeness, negation, agency, modality, doctrine, scripture; uncertainties: 0; model notes: part 1/5: [scripture] "Ps 133,1.2" vs "Ps 133,1.2": Should be Ps 134[133],1-2 (LXX 134 = Hebrew/English 133); comma should indicate range; [scripture] "Ps 134,1.2" vs "Ps 134,1.2": Should be Ps 135[134],1-2 (LXX 135 = Hebrew/English 134); comma should indicate range; [scripture] "Ps 134,3.4" vs "Ps 134,3.4": Should be Ps 135[134],3-4 (LXX 135 = Hebrew/English 134); comma should indicate range; [modality] "when neither day nor night will it cease" vs "ὡς μήτε ἡμέρας μήτε νυκτὸς διαλιπεῖν": Infinitive 'to leave uninterrupted' not future indicative; 'will cease' overstates modality; [agency] "just as David appointed the singers to remain for this purpose" vs "ὥσπερ καὶ κατέστησεν ἐπὶ τούτῳ μενοῦντας τοὺς ὑμνῳδοὺς ὁ ∆αυίδ": ἐπὶ τούτῳ = 'for this' not 'for this purpose'; μενοῦντας = 'remaining' not 'to remain' (purpose); [completeness] "though in creation he is God of all" vs "ἐν δημιουργίᾳ": Missing 'in creation' contrast with 'in intimacy'; 'though' adds adversative not in source | part 2/5: [source_identity] "the things at the Red Sea" vs "τὰ κατὰ τὴν ἐρυθράν": Missing 'Sea' in source citation; should be 'Red [Sea]' or 'Erythra'; [agency] "he is the one who once for all lifts up clouds" vs "αὐτός ἐστιν ὁ νεφέλας μετεωρίζων": Subject is God/creative authority, not 'he' ambiguous; 'once for all' overtranslates καθάπαξ; [completeness] "They are not known where they are before they blow" vs "οὐ πρότερον γινωσκομένων ἔνθα εἰσὶ πρὶν ἢ καὶ πνεύσωσι": Drops 'on the one hand'/'first' (πρότερον) contrast; 'they blow' should be 'they might blow' (subjunctive); [doctrine] "the unseen and unknown origin of the winds is God's treasury" vs "θεοῦ δὲ θησαυρὸν τὸ τῆς τῶν ἀνέμων γενέσεως ἀθεώρητον καὶ ἄγνωστον εἶναι λέγει": Reversed: source says 'God's treasury is the unseen/unknown [thing] of wind generation', not 'origin...is treasury'; [completeness] "as in the treasuries of bodies" vs "καθάπερ ἐν τοῖς σωμάτων ἔχει θησαυροῖς": Missing verb 'it has' (ἔχει); should be 'as bodies have treasuries' | part 3/5: [agency] "discrediting them by the material" vs "τῇ τε ὕλῃ διαβάλλων": τε is 'both,' not 'by the'; 'discrediting by the material' obscures that τε coordinates three parallel instruments; [completeness] "and by the workmanship, because they are made by humans" vs "καὶ τῇ ἐργασίᾳ καθαίρων ὅτι ὑπὸ ἀνθρώπων": καθαίρων means 'purifying/cleansing' (ironic: stripping away divinity), not 'because they are made'; [negation] "because there is no spirit of life in them" vs "διὰ τὸ μὴ ἐνεῖναι πνεῦμα ζωῆς ἐπ' αὐτοῖς": ἐπ' αὐτοῖς is 'upon them,' not 'in them'; preposition matters for locution; [completeness] "the open discredit of the worship and the open refutation of the demons" vs "τοῦ τε σεβάσματος ἔχει τὴν ἐξ ἐμφανοῦς διαβολὴν καὶ τῶν δαιμόνων τὸν κατὰ τὸ ἐμφανὲς ἔλεγχον": τε is 'both,' omitted; 'of the worship' lacks 'also/too' force; demons' refutation is parallel to worship's discredit; [modality] "that those whose likenesses are such things are not gods" vs "ὅτι μὴ θεοὶ ὧν τὰ τοιαῦτα ὁμοιώματα": μὴ with indicative is 'that not' (factual denial), but 'those whose' makes relative clause; ὧν is genitive of possession, 'of whom'; [doctrine] "the human being who is an image is the divine one, not the one deprived of the Godhead" vs "ἄνθρωπος εἰκὼν ὁ θεῖος, οὐχ ὁ τῆς θεότητος ἐστηρημένος": ὁ θεῖος is substantive 'the divine one' as predicate, not modifier; 'who is an image' inverts: 'human [is] image [of] the divine one' | part 4/5: [agency] "he sets down as a demonstration of God's mercy" vs "ἐλέου θεοῦ δεῖγμα τίθεται": Subject is not 'he' but the events themselves; 'τίθεται' is passive/middle, 'is placed/set down'; [completeness] "who gave their land to the Hebrews" vs "χώραν εἰς ἐνοίκησιν ἀγαθὴν παρέχοντος Ἑβραίοις τὴν ἐκείνων": Dropped 'ἐκείνων' (theirs); 'their land' not just 'land'; [negation] "For they would not have perished otherwise, had they not come" vs "οὐδὲ γὰρ αὖ ἑτέρως ἀπώλοντο ἂν μὴ οὐκ εἰς πλήρωσιν ἥκοντες": Double negative 'μὴ οὐκ' = 'if not'/'unless'; 'οὐδὲ' = 'not even/nor'; 'they would not have perished otherwise unless coming'—translation inverts logic; [agency] "Moses says that Israel did not take possession" vs "Μωυσῆς γέ φησιν οὐ διὰ τὰς αὐτοῦ δικαιοσύνας τὸν Ἰσραὴλ κεκρατηκέναι": Moses says Israel did not obtain through HIS (Moses's) righteousnesses, not 'his own' ambiguous; 'κεκρατηκέναι' = 'to have obtained/conquered', not 'take possession'; [modality] "the beneficent gift was loving" vs "φιλανθρώπινον τὴν εὐεργετικὴν δόσιν": Missing 'εἶναι'; 'was' should be 'is' or infinitive in indirect statement; [modality] "the piety of the fathers became a preparation" vs "παρασκευὴν γεγενῆσθαι τὴν τῶν πατέρων εὐσέβειαν": Infinitive γεγενῆσθαι in indirect statement; 'to have become/been made', not simple past 'became'; [scripture] "Ps 135,16®22" vs "271 Ps 135,16®22": Psalm citation: LXX Ps 135 = Heb/Eng Ps 136; should be Ps 136[135] | part 5/5: [agency] "they considered the foreign souls a foreign land" vs "ἀλλοτρίαν γῆν ἡγοῦντο τὰς ἀλλοτρίας ψυχάς": Subject is wrong: 'they' refers to Israelites, but Greek has no expressed subject; more importantly, the construction ἡγοῦντο τὰς ἀλλοτρίας ψυχὰς ἀλλοτρίαν γῆν means 'they regarded the foreign souls as a foreign land'—the English inverts the metaphor, making souls the land rather than treating souls as land.; [completeness] "and they guarded against bringing out the divine things among them" vs "καὶ φυλάττεσθαι δὲ ἐν τούτοις ἐκφέρειν τὰ θεῖα": Dropped 'ἐν τούτοις' ('in these [matters/circumstances]'); the English 'among them' changes meaning, suggesting among foreign souls rather than 'in these circumstances'.; [modality] "and they guarded against" vs "φυλάττεσθαι": Infinitive φυλάττεσθαι is passive 'to be guarded' or middle 'to guard oneself', not active 'they guarded'; the construction continues the indirect statement after ἡγοῦντο, so 'they considered it necessary to guard against' or 'they took care'—the English makes it a finite active verb with 'they' as subject, breaking the syntax.; [scripture] ""On the willows we hung up our instruments."" vs "Ἐπὶ ταῖς ἰτέαις ἐκρεμάσαμεν τὰ ὄργανα ἡμῶν": Psalm reference is 136:1-2 in LXX (137:1-2 Hebrew/English); the English translation gives no bracketed Hebrew number, but this is editorial not translational. However, the English 'instruments' for ὄργανα is acceptable. No actual defect here—withdrawn.
[glm @cf/zai-org/glm-5.2] verdict=fail; failed checks: completeness, agency; uncertainties: 0; model notes: part 3/5: [completeness] "and by the lifelessness along with the vanity of the likeness of souls" vs "τῷ ἀψύχῳ μετὰ τοῦ ματαίου τῶν ψυχῶν ὁμοιώματος": Dropped 'of souls' (τῶν ψυχῶν); reads 'likeness of souls' not just 'likeness'. | part 4/5: [completeness] "while toward these the beneficent gift was loving," vs "πρὸς δὲ τούτους φιλάνθρωπον τὴν εὐεργετικὴν δόσιν": φιλάνθρωπον ('benevolent/humane') is dropped; 'loving' wrongly back-translates the noun that governs the next clause instead.; [completeness] "and the piety of the fathers became a preparation for sharing in that love." vs "εἰς δὲ τὴν μετοχὴν τῆς φιλανθρωπίας παρασκευὴν γεγενῆσθαι τὴν τῶν πατέρων εὐσέβειαν": μετοχὴν τῆς φιλανθρωπίας = 'sharing in the benevolence'; 'that love' loses the article's reference to φιλανθρωπία above. | part 5/5: [agency] "and they guarded against bringing out the divine things among them" vs "καὶ φυλάττεσθαι δὲ ἐν τούτοις ἐκφέρειν τὰ θεῖα": Greek is an infinitive of obligation ('to be guarded was to bring out'), not 'they guarded against bringing out'; flips duty into avoidance.
Latin quote (from model note, verified): «ὡς μήτε ἡμέρας μήτε νυκτὸς διαλιπεῖν»
English quote (from model note, verified): «On the willows we hung up our instruments.»
ADJUDICATED @cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6 (Densify (agent), clause-by-clause check against the Greek, 2026-10-09): Checked each flag against the Greek; none is a meaning error. Fragment headings (Ps 133,1.2; 134,1.2; 134,3.4; 135,16-22) are the edition's LXX lemmata. οὐδὲ γὰρ αὖ ἑτέρως ἀπώλοντο ἂν μὴ οὐκ εἰς πλήρωσιν ἥκοντες = 'they would not have perished otherwise, had they not come to the fullness', as rendered. θεοῦ δὲ θησαυρὸν τὸ … ἀθεώρητον καὶ ἄγνωστον εἶναι = the unseen and unknown origin of the winds is God's treasury (same predication). 'they considered the foreign souls a foreign land' is the Greek's own order (ἀλλοτρίαν γῆν ἡγοῦντο τὰς ἀλλοτρίας ψυχάς). καὶ φυλάττεσθαι … ἐκφέρειν τὰ θεῖα continues that indirect statement ('and took care not to bring out the divine things among them'). The rest are particles, voice and aspect style.
ADJUDICATED @cf/zai-org/glm-5.2 (Densify (agent), clause-by-clause check against the Greek, 2026-10-09): Not meaning errors. 'the likeness of souls' keeps τῶν ψυχῶν. φιλάνθρωπον is rendered 'loving' (the gift toward these was loving), and τῆς φιλανθρωπίας is 'that love', referring back to it. φυλάττεσθαι … ἐκφέρειν τὰ θεῖα = 'to guard against bringing out the divine things' (middle φυλάττεσθαι + infinitive = take care not to), as rendered.
